solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Politician left overwhelmed by support for archbishop

indicators.note: something overwhelmed by another is swallowed up inside it, so the support encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician has turned against the archbishop, smothering the support he once gave.
explanation.walkthrough: William Temple was Archbishop of Canterbury in the 1940s, so the definition names a person, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: William Temple was a twentieth-century Archbishop of Canterbury, so the surname stands for a famous primate.

clue.text: His mouth is shut, ultimately having to keep quiet?

definitions.text: His mouth is shut, ultimately having to keep quiet?

indicators.note: the outer pieces keep the quiet letter inside

parts.note: trap is slang for mouth

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its last

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: A man whose lips are sealed, presumably because he must stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' signals the insertion. Read whole, the clue describes a monk of an order known for silence, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappist monks are known for keeping a rule of near-silence.

clue.text: Spoil preserve with inclusion of yellow seasoning

parts.note: to spoil is to mar

indicators.note: the preserve includes the colour inside it

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: Ruining a jar of jam by adding a yellow herb.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold, standing for yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Marjoram is a herb used to flavour food, an aromatic seasoning.

clue.text: No expert in revolutionary socialism

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters are read backwards
the letters sit in the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone who is no authority on radical left-wing politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds CIAL inside 'socialism', and 'revolutionary' turns it round. 'revolutionary socialism' reads as one political phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A layperson, not clergy or a specialist, is laic: lay, no professional.

clue.text: Performing Ring, hit bass lines of consistent depth

indicators.note: a piece being performed is put through its paces, so the following letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: An opera singer performing Wagner's Ring cycle belts out the bass lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performing' turns O (Ring) plus HITBASS into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: On a chart, contour lines joining points at the same water depth are called by this technical term.

clue.text: Resolute in desiring not to join union?

definitions.meaning: firm and determined, with one fixed aim
read as minded to stay single, unwilling to enter the union of marriage

explanation.surface: Someone determined to avoid joining a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union but is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fixed on a single aim is determination; read literally it is a wish to stay unmarried.

clue.text: Singer describes plant on the point of flowering?

definitions.meaning: a rock and roll singer of the 1950s

definitions.text: plant on the point of flowering?
definitions.meaning: an evergreen shrub in bud, about to bloom

explanation.surface: A singer is described as a plant about to blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'budding holly' for the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddy Holly was an American rock and roll star; split, it is a shrub in bud.

clue.text: Hearts of entire nation go to a new artist

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: The heart and soul of a whole country goes to a new painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was a great Venetian Renaissance painter.

clue.text: In which one sits up straight at first, getting confused

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to addle is to confuse; addled means muddled

explanation.surface: Being told to sit up straight leaves one muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sits up straight' reads as posture, but the definition is a rider's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits up on a horse in this leather seat.

clue.text: Skilful, detailed description of how the French drive?

indicators.note: read as de-tailed: the final letter of the French phrase is cut off

parts.words: description of how the French drive
parts.note: in France cars keep to the right, in French 'à droite'

explanation.surface: A clever account of driving habits across the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'thorough' but means the tail comes off: the French phrase A DROITE loses its last E.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deft and dexterous is to be skilful, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Without correction fluid I tend to get stuck in university education

indicators.note: one thing stuck in another is lodged inside it, so the jumbled letters go into the other pieces
fluid things shift shape, so I and TEND are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at university uses correction fluid, which keeps getting stuck to things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correction fluid' is a decoy pairing: 'fluid' is the anagram signal on I TEND, and 'stuck in' places the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Text left as first written has had no editing or correction applied.

clue.text: Large mob half-heartedly supports Dartmoor team?

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece goes beneath the others

parts.note: Dartmoor is an English prison, so its inmates are cons
a side is a team

indicators.note: half of the doubled heart letters is removed

parts.note: a mob is a rabble

explanation.surface: A large crowd turns out, half-heartedly, to support the prison team.
explanation.walkthrough: Dartmoor is a well-known prison in Devon, England, hence CON. 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two middle Bs of RABBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerable means sizeable or substantial, so it means large.

clue.text: Hooker's beginning to provoke one of his team-mates

parts.note: hooker is slang for a prostitute, shortened to pro

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rugby hooker starts winding up a team-mate.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the hooker packs down between two props in the scrum, so a prop is his team-mate; 'Hooker' in the wordplay is the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is a front-row forward in rugby union who binds beside the hooker in the scrum.

clue.text: Everyone is after pie of lovely British game

indicators.note: the last piece comes after the others in the answer
printer's pie is a jumble of spilled type, so the word after is mixed up

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: Everybody is after a slice of a lovely British pie.
explanation.walkthrough: Printer's pie is spilled, jumbled type, so 'pie' is the anagram signal; 'is after' fixes the order of the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Volleyball is a team sport, a ball game played over a high net.

clue.text: Rub up a curate the wrong way, being stickler for procedure

indicators.note: up as in mixed up: these letters are stirred
going the wrong way means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Annoying a clergyman by being a pedant about rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rub up the wrong way' is an idiom for annoy; here 'up' and 'the wrong way' rearrange RUB and ACURATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureaucrat is an official who insists on following rules and procedures rigidly.

clue.text: A Lotus (nothing less!) my boss ordered could, over time, become one

definitions.text: A Lotus (nothing less!) my boss ordered could, over time, become one

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go over, that is around, the abbreviation for time
ordered here means put in order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
less means without, so the zero is taken away

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: The boss's newly ordered Lotus sports car will in time be a sign of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes zero ('nothing'), 'ordered' rearranges what remains with MY BOSS, and 'over' wraps that round the time letter. Read whole, the clue also describes the car.
explanation.definitionFit: An expensive sports car is a classic possession bought to display wealth and prestige.

clue.text: An old lady keeps up appearance of managing land

parts.note: an gives the article A

indicators.note: the first pieces keep the reversed word inside them

parts.note: gran is grandmother, an old lady

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: A grandmother keeps up appearances while running the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the word for appearance, and 'keeps' holds it inside A GRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrarian describes matters relating to farmland and its cultivation.

clue.text: Style of performing musical upset censor

indicators.note: in a down answer upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Cats is a long-running musical
Cato the Elder was a famous Roman censor

explanation.surface: A theatre show offends the official censor.
explanation.walkthrough: Cato held the Roman office of censor; 'upset' looks like an anagram signal but reverses CATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is a musical performance style with short, detached notes.

clue.text: Hey, leaving sporting venue's easy without influential member

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the easy word goes round the rest

parts.note: light work is easy

indicators.note: the letters of hey leave the venue's name

parts.note: Headingley is a cricket and rugby ground in Leeds

explanation.surface: A shout goes up as someone leaves the stadium, where an important player was missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Headingley is a cricket ground in Leeds, England. 'leaving' removes the H, E and Y of 'Hey'; 'without' means outside, so the easy word goes round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent figure who guides others in an organisation is called this idiom.

clue.text: Affectionate love's outwardly displayed if you do this

definitions.text: Affectionate love's outwardly displayed if you do this

parts.note: affectionate means fond

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Caressing someone shows your affection openly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the action: affection shown outwardly by touch.
explanation.definitionFit: To fondle is to stroke or caress lovingly, an outward display of affection.

clue.text: Artist seen around one Welsh festival

indicators.note: the artist is seen around the other letters

parts.note: Salvador Dali, the Surrealist painter
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A painter is seen at a Welsh festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights.

clue.text: If you are quick they won't include you

definitions.text: If you are quick they won't include you

parts.words: If you are quick they won't include you
parts.note: quick in its old sense means alive, and only the dead appear in these newspaper notices

explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' seems to mean fast, but it is the old sense 'living', as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper death notices record people who have died, so the living are left out.

clue.text: Refuse stuff that's been sent back

indicators.note: something sent back goes the reverse way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: Turning down goods that have been returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is the pulpy residue of grapes after pressing, a kind of waste matter.

clue.text: Takes hard drug

parts.note: takes means has, as in has a meal
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone takes a hard drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash is short for hashish, cannabis resin.

clue.text: After help backward family attack

indicators.note: the family word follows the reversed help in the answer
the word for help is read backwards

parts.note: help means aid
a tribe is an extended family group

explanation.surface: A family, after their backward child was helped, goes on the offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a forceful denunciation.

clue.text: Posh car carrying police officer

indicators.note: the car carries the officer inside it

parts.note: Lada is a Russian make of car
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: An upmarket vehicle is ferrying a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase mocks affected upper-class manners, meaning pretentiously refined.

clue.text: Letters of complaint carrying weight following tip from advocate

indicators.note: the complaint piece follows the letter from the advocate
the tip here is the end, the final letter of the word
the complaint carries the weight inside it

parts.note: piles is an ailment, haemorrhoids
ST is stone, a British unit of weight

explanation.surface: Letters of complaint from a lawyer carry real weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' is the end, not the start: E. ST (stone) is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistles are formal letters, as in the New Testament letters of Paul.

clue.text: Mum gets enthusiastic about religion

parts.note: mum as in keep mum, a call for silence: sh
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: Mother has become keen on a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not mother but the call for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the indigenous religion of Japan.
